Hello {name}, I'm reaching out from Mehamakor — a directory platform for local businesses looking for repeat customers.

outreach.call_script:
1. Warm opening: "Hi, I'm calling from Mehamakor, is this a good time?"
2. Brief explanation: "An Israeli site connecting local businesses with shoppers seeking quality food."
3. Value proposition: "Registration is free, your profile will be published, and you receive direct inquiries from customers via WhatsApp."
4. Open question: "How does that sound?"
5. If interested: "Great! I'm sending you a ready link with all your details — just confirm a password."
6. If declined: "No problem, thanks for your time. If you change your mind, our address is mehamakor.online."
7. Closing: "Have a great day."

help.title: Admin help
help.intro: This guide summarises the admin panel tools, key approval processes, and incident responses. Maintained manually — if something here is wrong, open a PR with a fix rather than leaving the next direction in the dark.

dashboard.title: Dashboard overview
dashboard.p1: /admin — the main page. Four top metrics (users, businesses, events, open reports) + a weekly delta row beneath them.
dashboard.li1: Yellow pill on "Dashboard" in the sidebar — number of items awaiting approval (businesses + reports + flagged products + experiences). Refreshes on every internal navigation.
dashboard.li2: DAU 30-day chart — based on users.last_active_at which updates on every authenticated request (5-min throttle).
dashboard.li3: Top cities — aggregated from producer_page_views (rows without city are not counted).
dashboard.li4: Server health — average response time + requests per minute over the last hour. Per-process only (resets on every deploy).

producers.title: Approving and rejecting businesses
producers.li2: Click the business name → full details page, including licensing declarations, photos, and description.
producers.li3: To approve: click "Quick approve". The business moves to approved, appears on the homepage, and shows on the map.
producers.li4: To reject: "Reject" + a short reason that will be emailed to the business owner.
producers.li5: Edit (pencil): goes to /admin/producers/[id]/edit — all fields including "verified" / "recommended" / "availability status" / "primary contact method".
producers.footnote: A business does not need to be verified to be approved — verified adds a blue tag after you've checked licensing and identity, usually in a monthly audit.

users.title: Managing users
users.p1: /admin/users — search by email/name, filter by role.
users.li1: role: consumer / producer / admin — applied immediately, with no further confirmation.
users.li2: Block: a blocked login returns 403. The user doesn't know immediately, they only see a message on their next login attempt.
users.li3: Favorites: click the count next to a user to see the businesses they saved — useful for tracking suspicious activity.
users.footnote: Reminder: blocking is reversible, a role change affects the next JWT immediately. Do not promote a user to admin without verifying identity outside the system.

reviews.title: Reviews
reviews.p1: /admin/reviews — all reviews in a single list (newest first).
reviews.li1: Filter by rating (1–5) or free-text search across business/user/title/body.
reviews.li2: Deletion requires confirmation (window.confirm). After deletion the business's avg_rating and review count update automatically.
reviews.li3: Deletion is the correct pattern for: defamatory language, personal information, spam, a review about a different business.

reports.title: Reports
reports.li1: Resolve — close the report, optionally with a follow-up action (block / delete).
reports.li2: Hold — keeps it open but moves it to the bottom of the list. Use when more information is needed.
reports.li3: Ignore — close with no action, for reports that don't substantiate an issue.
reports.footnote: Rule of thumb: respond within 24 hours. Product-safety reports (allergens, expiration dates) — immediately.

experiences.title: Experiences
experiences.p1: /admin/experiences — 5 tabs: pending / changes required / approved / rejected / all.
experiences.li1: On click: approve / reject / request changes. The host receives an email.
experiences.li2: Haiku pre-check runs before an experience reaches the "pending" tab — the "changes required" tab is when the AI flagged a warning but did not block.

emergency.title: Emergencies
emergency.site_down_body: Check mehamakor.online/health. If it's not 200 OK, check Railway → healthcheck + logs. See CLAUDE.md §"Railway runtime port = 8080" before any debugging — this is the most common source of 502.
emergency.migration_body: Symptom: the container starts but endpoints return 500 with UndefinedColumn. Fix: verify that _migrate_columns in main.py lists the new column. If not, add it and push a hotfix commit.
emergency.login_broken_body: Verify that JWT_SECRET_KEY exists in Railway Variables. If it was changed by mistake — old JWTs are invalidated and every user has to log in again. Do not rotate the key without alerting the team.
emergency.spam_body: /register/producer is already rate-limited to 3/hour (slowapi). If that isn't enough, tighten to 1/hour temporarily in auth.py + hotfix push. Block suspicious IPs at Railway edge if traffic is unusual.
emergency.ai_silent_body: Check ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Fail-open is not infinite — if the key expired, moderation approves everything (APPROVED default). CLAUDE.md §"Anthropic client init" describes the httpx 0.28+ bug that may return TypeError via the green button.
